newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE says considering extension of trading hours.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE says considering extension of trading hours.

text.p: The Tokyo International Financial Futures Exchange (TIFFE) is considering extending trading hours to invigorate activity, a TIFFE official said on Tuesday.

Under the plan, the exchange would shorten its lunch break to an hour from the current 1-1/2 hours and bring forward the time of the break. The proposed new lunch break would run from 11.30 a.m. to 12.30 p.m. (0230 GMT to 0330 GMT) compared with the current 12.00 p.m. to 1.30 p.m, the official said.

Many market participants believe the move is designed to halt an outflow of activity to the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX), which also lists three-month euroyen futures, the main instrument traded at TIFFE.
But the official said this was not the aim.
"We don't have SIMEX on our minds, but the plan may end up doing this (halting the outflow)," he said.
The official said the exchange had begun discussions with its members over the plan and added that it would like to come up with a conclusion within a month. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk (81-3 5473 3710)
